_note: Per-dataset SPEC-CARD fields. These cards describe THE ATLAS, not the slice we happen to work on: `cells`, `schema` tier counts and `timepoints` are all full-published-object numbers, with `workingSlice` naming our subset where one exists. Joined on `id` to dataset_facts.json (still the source of truth for METHOD/platform and the cluster counts in the summary strip); dataset_facts.json is never modified. Values are read live from the backing .h5ad / author metadata, transcribed from repo prose, or supplied by Steven — see `_provenance`. Anything unsourced is the literal string "TBD". Where a field is not a gap but a genuine absence, it says so in words ("Unannotated — labelling target", "N/A") rather than TBD.

_provenance.cells_and_slices: Full-object n_obs read in backed mode. zscape 3,231,733 (obs[timepoint]==48 -> 813,782, matches facts.cells). daniocell 336,603 (36-72 hpf window -> 191,832, matches facts.cells). chemfish 2,068,668 (timepoint==48 -> 1,579,675, which is what facts.fullCells records; facts.cells 250,000 is our uniform sample of that). commit_gold 209,639 is the benchmark definition itself, not a subsample, so no working-slice line. megafin/megafin_parse/minifin are used whole.

Counts are NOT comparable across datasets — the tiers are different granularities, which is why the cards show the hierarchy rather than a normalised number.

_provenance.genome_annotation: VERIFIED: MegaFin ZSB = Lawson Lab v4.3 on GRCz11. The Lawson paper (PMC7486121) states the v4.3 annotation comprises 36,351 genes and assigns every gene an arbitrary 'LL' ID — our object has n_vars 36,351 and var[ll_id] of the form LL#########. Exact match, so this one is settled. MiniFin + MegaFin Parse = GRCz11 from process/run_proc_def.json (Parse split-pipe v1.7.1) and independently from the sequencing QC review (GRcZ11 used, not GRCz12, because the line is TU). NOT VERIFIED: ZSCAPE / ZSCAPE Commit Gold / ChemFish / DanioCell annotation is back to TBD. The earlier 'Lawson Lab v4.3.2' came from search snippets, and the SAME sentence surfaced for all three papers, which is a strong sign one source was being echoed rather than three independently confirming. Their gene universes (32,031 and 30,121) also do not match Lawson v4.3's 36,351, which would need explaining. Genome GRCz11 is still well-supported for all of them; only the GTF is unresolved.
_provenance.zebrahub_capture: Whole-cell, from Lange et al. 2024 (Cell) methods: an optimised cell-dissociation protocol avoiding embryo pooling, suspensions counted at 700-1200 cells/ul and loaded on the Chromium Controller. The nuclei-based protocol belongs to Zebrahub-Multiome, a different assay.
_provenance.zscape_groups: Grouping derived from the naming convention in obs[gene_target], NOT from a genotype column — none exists. '-mut' suffix = stable mutant line; a hyphen joining two gene symbols = double knockout; bare symbol = single-gene F0 crispant. Corroborated by the data: hgfa/hgfa-mut, mafba/mafba-mut, met/met-mut, noto/noto-mut, tbx16/tbx16-mut all appear as SEPARATE targets (which only makes sense as crispant vs mutant of the same gene), and four of the five mutant genes have a matching sibling control arm (ctrl-hgfa, ctrl-mafba, ctrl-met, ctrl-noto). 18 single + 5 double + 5 mutant = 28.
_provenance.chemfish_doses: Per-compound concentrations from cell_metadata dose/dose_type: Cyclopamine 100, DEAB 10, DMH1 40, LY411575 10, SB505124 50, SU5402 20, WntC59 20, A8301 50 (all micromolar). Each compound has exactly ONE concentration — unlike MegaFin, ChemFish is not a two-dose design. Dosing timepoints from obs[drug_addition] = 6/13/24/36/42 hpf; collection from obs[timepoint] = 36/48/72 hpf. Only the 6 and 13 hpf dosing arms were collected at all three timepoints; 24/36/42 hpf dosing was collected at 48 hpf only.

The object on this instance is missing wells B11, C3 and E3, i.e. Vorinostat 1 uM, Romidepsin 5 uM and Dinaciclib 5 uM; dataset_facts.json's `design` field names exactly those three. Steven's MegaFin write-up instead lists the failed samples as Dapagliflozin 1 uM (B7), Rivaroxaban 1 uM (B9) and Budesonide 5 uM (G10) — all three of which ARE present in our object. _provenance.annotation_evidence: ZSCAPE counting reference, SETTLED: GRCz11 with Ensembl release 99 (Danio_rerio.GRCz11.dna.toplevel.fa.gz / Danio_rerio.GRCz11.99.gtf.gz), prepared by the BBI genome pipeline — biotype exclusion then a strand-aware 3' extension of up to 500 bp with same-strand collision clipping — giving 32,031 ENSDARG genes. CODE: bbi-lab/bbi-genome-data (tree 946231a3). organisms/genome.zebrafish.sh names the release, FASTA and GTF; scripts/rna.03.make_bed_files.sh line 4 EXTENSION_LIST="500" and extend_3p_utr_gene_annotations() line 207 implement the extension and clipping. The 500 constant dates to 2020-03-20, predating the 2022-05 deposit. bbi-sci bin/assign-reads-to-genes.py consumes those BEDs. DATA: +strand 3' end median +500, -strand 3' start median -500, 5' ends median 0, max exactly 500 (mean 493 = clipped genes); Ensembl 99 minus pseudogene|IG_*|TR_*|TEC is an EXACT 32,031 set match, 0 discrepancies either way. LAWSON IS RULED OUT — tested directly against the published annotation (eLife 55792 Source Data 2, md5 19759898187c47edfd9c216162851e31, at raw_datasets/_annotations/lawson_v4_3/): 4.54% coordinate agreement (worse than plain Ensembl's 7.34%), bidirectional deltas, and 3,629 ZSCAPE gene ids absent from Lawson entirely. Not a plausible alternative; retained only as a closed negative result. UNRESOLVED: no ZSCAPE-specific run manifest naming the GTF exists — absent from the paper, the GEO series and per-sample records, the bbi-sci docs and the sdg-zfish repo. The transformation is RECONSTRUCTED to exact agreement; the historical manifest is not recovered. CHEMFISH INHERITS IT — CONFIRMED: its cds rowRanges mcols match ZSCAPE's gene metadata on all 32,031 genes for id, ORDER, gene_short_name, chromosome, bp1, bp2 and strand (100.0000%, 0 mismatches in any field). Its Methods independently state read processing and cell filtering followed Saunders et al. 2023. The literal FASTA/GTF filenames are STRONGLY INFERRED by that inheritance: the ChemFish object embeds no reference strings at all.
_provenance.pipeline: How the authors got from raw FASTQ to the object we hold. ZSCAPE — supplied by Steven with citations: bbi-dmux -> bbi-sci (Methods, Nature s41586-023-06720-2), Monocle3 v1.3.1, GEO GSE202639 / SRA SRP374541 / PRJNA836866, repo cole-trapnell-lab/sdg-zfish. That same table also states the GTF is NOT resolvable from the paper or GEO and that Ensembl-vs-Lawson cannot be justified for raw counting — which is why ZSCAPE's annotation stays TBD. GRCz11 downstream gene NAMES do not prove an Ensembl GTF was used for alignment. ChemFish — downstream confirmed LOCALLY, not from the web: the distribution is extracted/chemfish_cds/cds_object.rds with a bpcells_matrix_dir, i.e. a Monocle3 cell_data_set. Raw side unconfirmed; same lab and assay as ZSCAPE makes bbi-dmux/bbi-sci likely but that is inference, so it stays TBD. DanioCell — distributed as a Seurat object (DanioCell site + GEO GSE223922); code at farrelllab/2023_Sur. CellRanger version not confirmed, so raw stays TBD. Zebrahub — TBD. The only pipeline detail findable (Cell Ranger ARC 2.0.2 + Signac) belongs to Zebrahub-MULTIOME, a different assay from the scRNA atlas on this card. Same trap as the genome citation. MiniFin + MegaFin — Parse split-pipe v1.7.1 read from process/run_proc_def.json; downstream from the Trailmaker settings in the design docs (Seurat+Harmony for MiniFin; Seurat then Scanpy for MegaFin). The ZSB build diverges after split-pipe: manual Lawson denoise, then our own Harmony pass. ZSCAPE Commit Gold left TBD deliberately — it is a cut of the same published ZSCAPE data, so it would inherit bbi-dmux/bbi-sci + Monocle3, but that is Steven's call to make rather than mine to assume.
_provenance.zscape_cell_metadata: GSE202639_reference_cell_metadata.csv.gz — 1,241,018 cells x 25 columns, the wild-type REFERENCE arm. Carries per-cell cell_type_sub (~156), cell_type_broad (~98), tissue (33), germ_layer (6), major_group (4), timepoint (19 incl. one blank), expt (GAP13/14/16/18, HF4), embryo, 3D UMAP coords, and gene_target. Note gene_target here has only 7 values: the 6 ctrl-* arms plus tbx16-mut (9,004 cells) — i.e. the reference arm bundles one stable mutant line with the controls, which supports the crispant-vs-stable-mutant split the ZSCAPE card draws from the naming convention. The 28 knockouts live in the zperturb file, not this one.
_provenance.zscape_raw_counts: GSE202639_reference_raw_counts.RDS.gz — dgCMatrix 32,031 x 1,241,018, 523,335,834 non-zeros (98.68% sparse), integer counts max 2,391, 954,711,330 total UMIs, median 454 UMI/cell. Dimensions match the gene and cell metadata exactly. No attributes naming the annotation. File is DOUBLY gzipped (outer gzip around an already-compressed RDS): gunzip first, then readRDS. TWO GAPS CLOSED. (a) The 32,031-gene set is the REFERENCE, not a QC artifact: 951 genes have zero counts across all 1.24M cells and were retained, which an expression filter would not do. (b) The 489 Ensembl genes it omits are excluded by gene-model CLASS, not location or expression — 299 pseudogenes, 171 IG/TR receptor segments, 14 TEC, 5 other; 488 of 489 are on primary chromosomes and ZSCAPE keeps 462 genes on non-primary scaffolds, so it is not an assembly restriction. Dropping pseudogenes and rearranging immune-receptor segments is curation, not a stock Ensembl GTF — a third independent line of evidence (with the extended coordinates and the Ensembl-subset id space) for a curated extended-UTR annotation. Still no citation naming it. CAVEAT: gene metadata's num_cells_expressed is systematically HIGHER than the matrix supports (median ratio 1.0076, max 1.093, never lower across all 32,031 genes) despite both files claiming 1,241,018 cells. Recompute from the matrix if exact.
_provenance.zscape_supplementary: sources/supplementary/zscape-extra-metadata.xlsx — the paper's supplementary tables, 8 sheets. Highest-information single file in sources/. CONFIRMS THE PERTURBATION SPLIT FROM THE AUTHORS' OWN TABLE, not from naming convention: sheet 6_perturbation_info lists 28 rows using 'hgfa' / 'hgfa null', 'mafba' / 'mafba null', 'met' / 'met null', 'noto' / 'noto null', 'tbx16' / 'tbx16 null'. So obs[gene_target]'s '-mut' suffix IS the authors' stable NULL mutant line, and the sheet's 'Null Comparison (y/n)' column is 'y' on exactly those five crispant rows. 18 single + 5 double + 5 null = 28 labels = 23 distinct perturbations. Card group relabelled 'Stable null mutant line' to match the authors' term. TIMEPOINTS: sheet 1 gives four experiments — Time Series R1 (48/72/96), R2 (18-38 even, +42), R3 (40/42/44/46), and the perturbation experiment (18/24/36/48/72). Their union is EXACTLY the 18 numeric values in obs[timepoint], and the perturbation timepoints are a subset. The abstract's '19 timepoints' is still one more than any file accounts for — likely the blank level in the reference cell metadata. ALSO: hash enrichment thresholds (>3 for R1/R2, >5 for perturbations and R3) — this is the 'Supplementary Table 1' the Methods cite; 76 crRNA sequences over 27 gene entries (3 non-targeting controls), ~3 guides/gene, 7 failed phenotyping and 10 unused so the shipped pool is 66; rhAmpSeq genotyping primers for 26 genes; per-perturbation cell and individual counts (smallest is tbx16 null at 7,475 cells / 8 individuals). NAMING: obs writes 'wnt3a-wnt8' but the real second gene is wnt8a ('wnt3a; wnt8a'). Card chips keep the literal obs strings because that is what the data column contains. SCHEME vs DATA: sheet 2 documents the authored annotation scheme (36 tissue / 101 broad / 148 sub / 7 germ_layer) which does NOT equal the values realized in obs (34 / 99 / 156 / 7). Neither is wrong — different denominators. Card numbers stay measured from the data. MOST USEFUL TO US: sheet 2 carries a free-text 'evidence' column naming the marker genes behind each cell-type call (120 of 151 rows), and sheet 8 gives quantitative top markers for 151 cell_type_sub values. That is a far richer scoring target for the labeller than the label strings alone.
_provenance.chemfish_pipeline: CONFIRMED from the ChemFish Methods: 'Pipelines for generating count matrices from sci-RNA-seq3 sequencing data are available at github.com/bbi-lab/bbi-dmux and github.com/bbi-lab/bbi-sci', and 'data were processed using the Monocle3 (develop branch, v.1.3.1) workflow'. _provenance.daniocell: REFERENCE CONFIRMED from the Methods: GRCz11 / Ensembl release 99 with the Lawson Lab Zebrafish Transcriptome Annotation v4.3.2, 320 Ensembl-annotated pseudogenes removed, aligned with Cell Ranger 4.0.0 (STAR 2.5.1b), --expect-cells 6,000-21,250 per sample. New data is 10X Chromium 3' v3.1 + MULTI-seq; the 2018 Farrell Drop-seq cells were realigned against the same reference before merging. This is a DIFFERENT reference lineage from ZSCAPE/ChemFish — its 36,250 features do not correspond to their BBI-prepared 32,031. GENE UNIVERSE RECONSTRUCTED against the Lawson v4.3 we hold (v4.3.2 is UMass-only and bot-walled): v4.3 has 36,351 gene rows, 314 with an Ens99 pseudogene biotype (paper removes 320 in v4.3.2), leaving 36,031 vs the released 36,250 (+219). Cell Ranger feature-name de-duplication explains the shape: Lawson has 216 symbols occurring more than once over 458 rows, and exactly 242 DanioCell-only names are '<lawson symbol>.N' (e.g. 'HTRA2 (1 of many).10'); 32 more differ only by case. The residual 2,006 is the v4.3->v4.3.2 delta. QC VERIFIED CLEAN, unlike ChemFish: 0 cells with nGene<=200 (min exactly 201), 0 cells with percent.mt>=10 (max 9.999), no Doublet label present (only Bar1-Bar12 and Negative), 1 cell with nUMI_MS<20. The top-0.5%-features rule is not testable post-hoc. 59,013 cells lack MULTI-seq calls: 38,731 Drop-seq plus 20,282 non-hashed 10X. ACCOUNTING: 489,687 was a header-inclusive line count, real total 489,686. 63 distinct integer stages in the release (Drop-seq 10 at 3-12 hpf, 10X 53 at 14-120 hpf, no overlap) vs the paper's 62 — one unit, UNRESOLVED. 522 clust in metadata vs 521 annotation rows: 'ceph' (3,191 cells) is unannotated, so annotation covers 99.348% of cells. 498 clust and 19 tissues are the 18-96 hpf subset, not alternative atlas figures. CANONICAL CONVERSION UNRESOLVED: no script exists on the instance, and the README's '26,251 mapped' does not reproduce — the on-box gene_id_map_zf.tsv (31,312 entries) intersects DanioCell at 27,247, and neither equals the 30,121 features actually in daniocell_canonical.h5ad. All 30,121 do fall inside the ZSCAPE 32,031 space, so the conversion targeted it, but the mapping is not recorded. Regenerate with a logged conversion before depending on its exact gene set. CITATION CORRECTED: the dataset README cited Nature Communications 10.1038/s41467-024-50053-5, which Crossref 404s — the DOI does not exist. Correct venue is Developmental Cell 58, 3028-3047.e12 (2023), 10.1016/j.devcel.2023.11.001, PMID 37995681.

zscape_commit_gold.name: ZSCAPE Commit Gold
zscape_commit_gold.summary: The Commit benchmark cut: ZSCAPE's published 112-cluster gold set at 48 hpf, control arm only. Clustering is given and frozen, so three personalities label each fixed cluster from a ZFA option menu and score by exact ZFA-ID match. Not blind — we hold the answer key on-instance.

reference.extension: +500 bp 3′, strand-aware — clipped where it would overlap a same-strand gene
reference.confidence: inherited: Commit Gold is a cut of the same published ZSCAPE data and carries the identical 32,031-gene feature universe.

zscape.name: ZSCAPE
zscape.summary: The Trapnell-lab whole-embryo knockout atlas: 28 gene knockouts against six control arms, spanning 18 to 96 hpf. We re-cluster from scratch with recursive per-compartment clustering, then score our de-novo names against the authors' published germ-layer, tissue, broad and sub labels.

reference.extension: +500 bp 3′, strand-aware — clipped where it would overlap a same-strand gene
reference.confidence: pipeline reconstruction + exact feature/coordinate fingerprint. No ZSCAPE-specific run manifest naming the GTF recovered.

chemfish.name: ChemFish
chemfish.summary: Barkan et al. chemical-screen atlas — eight pathway-blocking compounds across three timepoints, hitting Hedgehog, retinoic acid, BMP, Notch, TGF-β, FGF and Wnt. We re-cluster the 48 hpf window de-novo and score against the authors' native tissue and cell-type labels.

reference.extension: +500 bp 3′, strand-aware — clipped where it would overlap a same-strand gene
reference.confidence: ChemFish's own BPCells row_names are byte-identical to ZSCAPE's 32,031-gene set. Coordinates not independently re-tested; same lab, same assay, same reference build.

daniocell.name: DanioCell
daniocell.summary: Farrell-lab dense developmental reference: 489,686 cells over 63 stages from 3 to 120 hpf, nothing perturbed. 10X Chromium plus realigned 2018 Drop-seq, MULTI-seq hashed. Populations are in-situ-validated, and 521 clusters carry author annotations with ZFA ontology IDs.

reference.processing: Cell Ranger mkref · 320 Ensembl pseudogenes removed
reference.extension: none — Cell Ranger default, no 3′ extension
reference.confidence: stated directly in the Methods. Distinct reference lineage from ZSCAPE/ChemFish — Lawson v4.3.2 via Cell Ranger, not the BBI Ensembl-99 +500 bp build, so the 36,250 features do NOT correspond to their 32,031.
